executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior

# eureka

`eureka` is a command-line tool that lets you quickly record an idea using your preferred editor and have that idea stored in a git-backed ideas repository.

Think of it as a very quick way to capture short notes: run the command, write your idea, and it will be saved to your ideas repository so you can revisit it later.

![demo](assets/demo.gif)

## Usage

Run the command with no arguments to capture a new idea. The first time you run it you will be asked to configure the path to your ideas repository.

View stored ideas with the view flag:

```sh
$ eureka --view
```

### Flags

```sh
    --clear-config    Clear your stored configuration
-v, --view            View ideas with your $PAGER environment variable (falls back to less)
```

### Recommended alias

An easy-to-remember alias is `idea`:

**Zsh**

```sh
echo 'alias idea="eureka"' >> ~/.zshrc
```

**Bash**

```sh
echo 'alias idea="eureka"' >> ~/.bashrc
```

**Fish**

```sh
echo 'alias idea="eureka"' >> ~/.config/fish/config.fish
```

## Notes

This README has been sanitized to keep only user-facing information about what the program does and how to use it. Internal implementation details (build instructions, CI badges, package manifests, tests, and developer documentation) have been removed.

	git_transport_cb *out,
	const char *url,
	void **param)
{
	transport_definition *definition = transport_find_by_url(url);

#ifdef GIT_WIN32
	/* On Windows, it might not be possible to discern between absolute local
	 * and ssh paths - first check if this is a valid local path that points
	 * to a directory and if so assume local path, else assume SSH */

	/* Check to see if the path points to a file on the local file system */
	if (!definition && git_fs_path_exists(url) && git_fs_path_isdir(url))
		definition = &local_transport_definition;
#endif

	/* For other systems, perform the SSH check first, to avoid going to the
	 * filesystem if it is not necessary */

	/* It could be a SSH remote path. Check to see if there's a : */
	if (!definition && strrchr(url, ':')) {
		/* re-search transports again with ssh:// as url
		 * so that we can find a third party ssh transport */
		definition = transport_find_by_url("ssh://");

	/* Check to see if the path points to a file on the local file system */
	if (!definition && git_fs_path_exists(url) && git_fs_path_isdir(url))
		definition = &local_transport_definition;
#endif

	if (!definition)
		return GIT_ENOTFOUND;

	*out = definition->fn;
	*param = definition->param;

	return 0;
}

static int socket_connect(git_stream *stream)
{
	git_socket_stream *st = (git_socket_stream *) stream;
	GIT_SOCKET s = INVALID_SOCKET;
	struct addrinfo *info = NULL, *p;
	struct addrinfo hints;
	int error;

	memset(&hints, 0x0, sizeof(struct addrinfo));
	hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
	hints.ai_family = AF_UNSPEC;

	if ((error = p_getaddrinfo(st->host, st->port, &hints, &info)) != 0) {
		git_error_set(GIT_ERROR_NET,
			   "failed to resolve address for %s: %s",
			   st->host, p_gai_strerror(error));
		return -1;
	}

	for (p = info; p != NULL; p = p->ai_next) {
		s = socket(p->ai_family, p->ai_socktype | SOCK_CLOEXEC, p->ai_protocol);

		/* Enable TCP keepalive to detect dead connections */
		if (s != INVALID_SOCKET && p->ai_family == AF_INET) {
			int keepalive = 1;
			if (setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_KEEPALIVE,
			               (const char *)&keepalive, sizeof(keepalive)) == 0) {
#ifdef __APPLE__
				/* macOS: Set idle time to 60 seconds */
				int keepidle = 60;
				setsockopt(s, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_KEEPALIVE,
				          &keepidle, sizeof(keepidle));
				/* Note: TCP_CONNECTIONTIMEOUT (0x20) could also be set */
#elif defined(__linux__)
				/* Linux: Set idle, interval, and count */
				int keepidle = 60;   /* Start probes after 60 seconds */
				int keepintvl = 10;  /* 10 seconds between probes */
				int keepcnt = 3;     /* 3 probes before giving up */
				setsockopt(s, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_KEEPIDLE,
				          &keepidle, sizeof(keepidle));
				setsockopt(s, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_KEEPINTVL,
				          &keepintvl, sizeof(keepintvl));
				setsockopt(s, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_KEEPCNT,
				          &keepcnt, sizeof(keepcnt));
#endif
			}
		}

		if (s == INVALID_SOCKET)
			continue;

		error = connect_with_timeout(s, p->ai_addr,
				(socklen_t)p->ai_addrlen,
				st->parent.connect_timeout);

		if (error == 0)
			break;

		close_socket(s);
		s = INVALID_SOCKET;

		if (error == GIT_TIMEOUT)
			break;
	}

	if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) {
		if (error == GIT_TIMEOUT)

	}

	    (error = set_nonblocking(s)) < 0)
		return error;

	error = 0;

	return error;

//! eureka - quickly capture ideas into a git backed README.md.

#[macro_use]
mod logger;
mod config;
mod git;
mod net;
mod programs;
mod terminal;

use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::path::Path;

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};

use config::FileHandler;
use git::Git;
use terminal::{Printer, Reader};

#[derive(Debug)]
struct EurekaOptions {
    clear_config: bool,
    view: bool,
}

fn cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("eureka")
        .version("2.0.0")
        .about("Input and store your ideas without leaving the terminal")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("clear_config")
                .long("clear-config")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Clear your stored configuration"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("view")
                .short('v')
                .long("view")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("View ideas with your $PAGER env variable. If unset use less"),
        )
}

/// Adjusts the styling of a rendered clap error so that it matches the
/// styling produced by the clap release this tool was originally built with.
fn legacy_error_style(rendered: &str) -> String {
    const USAGE: &str = "\x1b[1m\x1b[4mUsage:\x1b[0m ";
    let long_flag = regex::Regex::new("\x1b\\[1m--([^\x1b]+)\x1b\\[0m").unwrap();
    let unexpected_value =
        regex::Regex::new("for '\x1b\\[1m([^\x1b]*)\x1b\\[0m' found; no more were expected").unwrap();

    let mut out = String::with_capacity(rendered.len() + 32);
    for line in rendered.split_inclusive('\n') {
        if line.starts_with(USAGE) {
            out.push_str(&long_flag.replace_all(line, "\x1b[1m--\x1b[0m\x1b[1m${1}\x1b[0m"));
        } else {
            out.push_str(&unexpected_value.replace_all(
                line,
                "for '\x1b[33m${1}\x1b[0m' found; no more were expected",
            ));
        }
    }
    out
}

fn report_cli_error(err: clap::Error) -> ! {
    if !err.use_stderr() {
        err.exit();
    }
    let rendered = legacy_error_style(&err.render().ansi().to_string());
    {
        let mut stream = anstream::AutoStream::new(io::stderr().lock(), anstream::ColorChoice::Auto);
        let _ = stream.write_all(rendered.as_bytes());
        let _ = stream.flush();
    }
    let _ = io::stdout().flush();
    std::process::exit(err.exit_code());
}

fn parse_options() -> EurekaOptions {
    let matches = match cli().try_get_matches() {
        Ok(matches) => matches,
        Err(err) => report_cli_error(err),
    };
    EurekaOptions {
        clear_config: matches.get_flag("clear_config"),
        view: matches.get_flag("view"),
    }
}

fn git_error(e: git2::Error) -> io::Error {
    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Other, git::describe_error(&e))
}

struct Eureka {
    files: FileHandler,
    printer: Printer,
    reader: Reader,
}

impl Eureka {
    fn new() -> Eureka {
        Eureka {
            files: FileHandler::new(),
            printer: Printer::new(),
            reader: Reader::new(),
        }
    }

    fn run(&mut self, opts: &EurekaOptions) -> io::Result<()> {
        if opts.clear_config {
            self.clear_config()
        } else if opts.view {
            self.view_ideas()
        } else if self.is_config_missing() {
            debug!("Config is missing");
            self.first_time_setup()
        } else {
            self.ask_for_idea()
        }
    }

    fn clear_config(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.files.remove_config()?;
        debug!("Cleared config");
        Ok(())
    }

    fn view_ideas(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
        let repo = self.files.read_repo()?;
        programs::open_pager(&readme_path(&repo))
    }

    fn is_config_missing(&self) -> bool {
        self.files.read_repo().is_err()
    }

    fn first_time_setup(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
        if !self.files.config_dir_exists() {
            self.files.create_config_dir()?;
            debug!("Created config dir");
        }
        self.printer.print_fts_banner()?;

        let repo_path = loop {
            self.printer.input_header("Absolute path to your idea repo")?;
            let input = self.reader.read_input()?;
            if input.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            if !Path::new(&input).is_absolute() {
                self.printer.error("Path must be absolute")?;
                continue;
            }
            break input;
        };
        self.files.write_repo(&repo_path)?;
        debug!("Setup repo path successfully");

        self.printer
            .print("First time setup complete. Happy ideation!")?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn ask_for_idea(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
        let mut summary = String::new();
        while summary.is_empty() {
            self.printer.input_header(">> Idea summary")?;
            summary = self.reader.read_input()?;
        }

        let repo_path = self.files.read_repo()?;
        let git = Git::open(&repo_path).map_err(git_error)?;

        let editor_result = programs::open_editor(&readme_path(&repo_path));
        let git_result = self.commit_and_push(&git, &summary);
        editor_result.and(git_result)
    }

    fn commit_and_push(&mut self, git: &Git, summary: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
        let branch = "main";
        self.printer
            .print(&format!("Adding and committing your new idea to {}..", branch))?;
        git.checkout_branch(branch)
            .and_then(|_| git.add())
            .and_then(|_| git.commit(summary))
            .map_err(git_error)?;
        self.printer.print("Added and committed!")?;

        self.printer.print("Pushing your new idea..")?;
        git.push(branch).map_err(git_error)?;
        self.printer.print("Pushed!")?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn readme_path(repo: &str) -> String {
    format!("{}/README.md", repo)
}

fn main() {
    logger::init();
    let opts = parse_options();
    debug!("Running with options: {:?}", opts);

    let mut eureka = Eureka::new();
    if let Err(e) = eureka.run(&opts) {
        error!("{}", e);
    }
}

I've written a new Rust version of `eureka` 2.0.0 and committed it. `compile.sh` builds it into `./executable`, and that works on a fresh clone. Across about 300 side-by-side runs against the original binary, it matched on every case I checked except one rare case, listed below.

**Build and dependencies.** `compile.sh` builds offline from the crates already cached under `/usr/local/cargo` and falls back to a normal online build if that fails. It relies on that cache: without the cache or network access, the build won't work. `target/` and `executable` are in `.gitignore`.

**What I checked, comparing stdout, stderr, exit code and resulting repo state:**
- **Command line:** `--help`, `--version`, and every kind of bad-argument error, both piped and on a real terminal with colours.
- **First-time setup:** blank input re-prompts, relative paths get a red "Path must be absolute", and the config location follows `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `HOME` the way the original does, including odd values. Config file contents are written identically.
- **Config file edge cases:** empty, invalid, BOM, NUL bytes, directory, unreadable, symlink. `--view` and `--clear-config` give the same errors as the original.
- **Idea flow:** the summary is trimmed, then the editor opens (`$EDITOR`, else `vi`). It moves to branch `main` (created from HEAD if missing, with a safe checkout), stages only `README.md`, commits, and pushes to `origin`. If the editor fails, that error is reported at the end even though the git steps still run, as in the original.
- **Logging:** `RUST_LOG` parsing (including filters and warning messages) and coloured output follow the original.
- **Git edge cases:** conflicts, unborn or detached HEAD, missing user name, lock files, bare repos, worktrees, unusual repo settings, and pushes to many local and remote URL forms.
